english: Two players $A$ and $B$ throw a fair die alternately, $A$ throwing first. $A$ wins the game the moment $A$ throws a $6$, and $B$ wins the game the moment $B$ throws a $5$ or a $6$; in addition, whichever player throws a $1$ loses the game at once, the other player being the winner. The throws continue until the game is decided, and the loser then pays the winner Rs. $60$. Then the expected gain, in rupees, of $A$ is ______.
hindi: दो खिलाड़ी $A$ तथा $B$ बारी-बारी से एक अनभिनत पासा फेंकते हैं, पहले $A$ फेंकता है। जैसे ही $A$ के पासे पर $6$ आता है, $A$ खेल जीत जाता है, तथा जैसे ही $B$ के पासे पर $5$ या $6$ आता है, $B$ खेल जीत जाता है; इसके अतिरिक्त, जिस भी खिलाड़ी के पासे पर $1$ आता है वह तुरन्त खेल हार जाता है और दूसरा खिलाड़ी विजेता होता है। खेल का निर्णय होने तक फेंकना जारी रहता है, तथा फिर हारने वाला विजेता को Rs. $60$ देता है। तब $A$ का अपेक्षित लाभ (रुपयों में) ______ है।
solution: $A$'s throw: $A$ wins $\frac16$, $B$ wins $\frac16$, game goes on $\frac23$. $B$'s throw: $B$ wins $\frac13$, $A$ wins $\frac16$, goes on $\frac12$
In one round ($A$ then $B$): $P(A\text{ wins in the round})=\dfrac16+\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac16=\dfrac5{18}$; $P(\text{round undecided})=\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac12=\dfrac13$
solution_full: On a throw by $A$: a $6$ (probability $\frac16$) ends the game in $A$'s favour, a $1$ (probability $\frac16$) ends it in $B$'s favour, and $2,3,4,5$ (probability $\frac46=\frac23$) pass the turn to $B$.
On a throw by $B$: $5$ or $6$ (probability $\frac13$) ends it in $B$'s favour, a $1$ (probability $\frac16$) ends it in $A$'s favour, and $2,3,4$ (probability $\frac12$) pass the turn back to $A$.

Call one throw by $A$ followed (if needed) by one throw by $B$ a round. $A$ wins during a round with probability $\dfrac16+\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac16=\dfrac{5}{18}$, and the round leaves the game undecided with probability $\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac12=\dfrac13$.
Rounds are independent, so $A$ wins in round $k+1$ with probability $\left(\dfrac13\right)^k\dfrac{5}{18}$. Summing the geometric series: $P(A)=\dfrac{5}{18}\cdot\dfrac{1}{1-\frac13}=\dfrac5{12}$.

Similarly $B$ wins during a round with probability $\dfrac16+\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac13=\dfrac7{18}$, so $P(B)=\dfrac7{18}\cdot\dfrac32=\dfrac7{12}$. Since $\dfrac5{12}+\dfrac7{12}=1$, the game ends with probability $1$.
$A$ gains Rs. $60$ with probability $\dfrac5{12}$ and loses Rs. $60$ with probability $\dfrac7{12}$: expected gain $=60\cdot\dfrac{5}{12}-60\cdot\dfrac{7}{12}=-10$.
originality_note: New: an alternating game in which each throw has three outcomes (win, immediate loss, continue) with different rules for the two players, so a round must be analysed as a unit before the geometric series over rounds (way 5: GP sum linked with a turn-based probability). Closest known: 'A and B throw a die alternately; the first to throw a 6 wins' (NCERT/JEE Main). Different because: a throw can also end the game against the thrower and the two players have different winning faces, so the one-step ratio 5/6 x 5/6 is replaced by a round analysis with cross terms.
blueprint_concepts: Probability problems requiring recursion or an infinite series

concept_use.Geometric Progression (GP) & Sum of GP: The probabilities of A winning in rounds 1, 2, 3, ... form a GP with ratio 1/3, summed to 5/12.
concept_use.Probability problems requiring recursion: The game is analysed by rounds: the probability that a round leaves the game undecided (1/3) is the ratio of an infinite series of probabilities.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, progression and function is introduced before use, all conditions are stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (sympy/fractions, brute force or simulation), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Used 'whichever player' and 'the moment A throws' to keep the stem gender-neutral and unambiguous. Simulation (200000 games) gave a mean gain of about -10.04. Changed: No change.
key_step: Treating one round as the unit (A wins 5/18, undecided 1/3) before summing the geometric series.
justification: Standard alternating-turn GP idea with an extra outcome per throw and asymmetric rules; two ideas linked, numerical. Level 3 like 2023-P2-Q2 (L3).
